---
title: "Errors in Quarto"
format: html
---

Usually, when rendering a Quarto document, if a code chunk has an error, it will stop the rendering process and print out that error.

Sometimes (rarely, but sometimes), you might want to include code with an error in the rendered document. This is usually just for demonstration, to show something not working as an example.

If you want to tell Quarto to not stop the rendering process, and instead just print out the error message under the cell, you can use a code chunk **execution option.**

To specify an option in a code chunk use the syntax `#|` and then specify the option. For telling a chunk to error, use the `error: true` setting. 

```{r}
#| error: true
1 + 1asfiasfkas
```

More code chunk execution options are documented here: [Execution Options](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/execution-options.html).
